listing_view.reasoning: Subscription reached only ~0.61x by late on day two of a three-day issue, which is weak for a mainboard IPO and suggests the issue may limp to full subscription on day-three QIB/HNI flows rather than genuine demand. Nothing in what I was given indicates pricing comfort: there is no basis-for-price chapter, no GMP, no anchor data, so weak demand is the only demand evidence I have.

longterm_view.reasoning: Reported profits look handsome (PAT margins 18-25%) but operating cash flow was negative ₹1,970m and ₹3,186m in the two latest years after a positive ₹11,019m, and receivable days ballooned from 35 to 137 — the 'profit' is substantially uncollected paper. ROE has fallen to 7.6% and RoCE to 10.6% while revenue shrank 24% in the latest year, so the earnings quality and the growth story are both deteriorating at the time of the ask.

governance.reasoning: The company is a SEBI-registered Investment Adviser that has received a SEBI show cause notice (June 30, year truncated) and a fresh SCN SEBI/HO/EAD/EAD3 in 2025, plus a ₹4 lakh SEBI penalty already paid [litigation, page 608, 610]. Multiple regulatory actions against the issuer and promoters, in a company regulated by SEBI itself, is a real governance discount, not boilerplate.

key_risks.risk: Earnings are not converting to cash
key_risks.why_it_matters: Two straight years of negative operating cash flow against large reported PAT means the P&L may overstate economic earnings, and the trend is worsening.
Customers taking four times longer to pay than two years ago raises collectability and channel-stuffing questions right before the IPO.
An open SEBI show cause notice and a paid penalty against a SEBI-regulated entity can escalate into licence or business restrictions.
RoCE of 10.6% and falling means incremental capital earns barely above borrowing cost, undercutting any justification for a growth-company multiple.
At ~0.61x on day two, listing-day performance depends on late institutional fills and carries a real risk of a weak or discounted debut.

answers.question: where did the money go — receivables, inventory, or both?
answers.answer: Receivables, demonstrably: collection stretched from 35.3 to 137.2 days over two years, which is the noted balance-sheet movement. Whether inventory also absorbed cash cannot be established — no inventory line was given.

answers.question: who are the customers, and is any of it disputed?
answers.answer: Not answerable from what I was given. No customer names, concentration data, or disputed-receivable disclosure appears in the extracts; the only signal is that someone is paying 137 days late.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the receivables are from creditworthy counterparties and were collected post-balance-sheet date, plus disclosure resolving the SEBI SCN, would materially improve the view; conversely, confirmation that the cash-flow gap is structural would push long-term well below 30.
